items.criterion: Use Google Search to locate Gemini API documentation (attempt and navigation)
items.description: Agent uses Google Search (without signing in) to find and open a result that appears to be official Gemini API documentation. Full credit if the agent demonstrates a reasonable search attempt (queries and selecting a relevant result) even if search results vary, or if Google Search is blocked (consent wall/CAPTCHA/outage) and the agent clearly reports the issue and proceeds via a reasonable alternative navigation path to an official Google documentation page. Partial credit if the agent reaches relevant Gemini documentation but the use of Google Search is not clearly demonstrated. No credit if the agent does not attempt search/navigation and does not reach Gemini API documentation.

items.criterion: Documentation source is an official Google domain and no sign-in is performed
items.description: The final documentation page used as the source is hosted on an official Google-owned domain (e.g., ai.google.dev, google.dev, developers.google.com, cloud.google.com). Full credit if the domain is official and the agent does not sign in. If a login prompt or consent screen appears, full credit as long as the agent avoids signing in and either proceeds without login or reports that access is blocked. No credit if the source is non-Google/non-official or the agent signs in.

Agent reports the title of the specific official documentation page they opened. Full credit if the title is exact or clearly identifies the opened page (minor formatting differences acceptable). Partial credit if the title is approximate/ambiguous but still plausibly refers to the opened page. No credit if missing or clearly unrelated.

Agent reports the domain (host) of the official documentation page used (or provides a full URL from which the domain is clearly inferable). Full credit if correct. Partial credit if only a full URL is provided but the correct domain is inferable. No credit if missing or incorrect.

items.criterion: Identify the Python SDK shown in the documentation example
items.description: Agent identifies the Python SDK/library shown in the Python example on the opened official documentation page (e.g., the package/import name). Full credit if it matches what is shown on that page at the time. If the page has no Python example (due to page changes/variant), full credit if the agent navigates within the same official docs to a Gemini API page that does show a Python example and reports the SDK from there, or clearly reports that no Python example is present/visible. Partial credit if the agent names the broader SDK family but not the exact library name. No credit if missing or incorrect without evidence of attempt.

items.criterion: Identify the model used in the Python example
items.description: Agent reports the exact model identifier used in the Python example on the opened official documentation page. Full credit if the model string matches what is shown on that page at the time. If the Python snippet/model is not visible due to page changes, full credit if the agent finds another official Gemini API doc page that contains a Python example and reports the model used there, or explicitly reports that the model cannot be determined from the visible example. Partial credit for a close but not exact model variant. No credit if missing or incorrect without evidence of attempt.

items.criterion: Stop after opening the official documentation and recording required fields
items.description: Agent stops browsing once it has opened official documentation and recorded the required fields (page title, domain, Python SDK, and example model). Full credit if the agent does not continue beyond what is needed. Partial credit if minor extra navigation occurs solely to locate the Python example within official docs. No credit if the agent significantly continues past the stopping condition or violates constraints (e.g., creates an API key, runs code, signs in).
